title_he: אָבִינוּ, אַהֲבָתְךָ הַבָּרָה קִבְּצָה אוֹתָנוּ סְבִיב הַמָּשִׁיחַ
review: The five-syllable refrain כָּבוֹד לִשְׁמֶךָ closes all six stanzas, as مَجْدًا لِاسْمِكَ does; it is not varied, because the Hebrew's short line is the tune's cadence and the stanza's whole point is that the name is the same throughout.

1:2 מֵעוֹלָם — the Arabic مُنْذُ الْأَزَل is 'from eternity'; עוֹלָם with מִן is the biblical idiom (Ps 93:2, מֵעוֹלָם), kept rather than the later קַדְמוּת so the line stays inside the psalm's vocabulary.

2:1–2 אַהֲבָה בָּרָה … סְבִיב הַמָּשִׁיחַ — the Arabic حُبُّكَ الصَّرِيح is 'Your plain/clear love'; בָּרָה is the 'pure, clear' adjective of Ps 19:9 (בָּרָה) and Song 6:9, so 'plain' becomes 'unmixed' and the gathering is round a person, not round a doctrine. The construct-free אַהֲבָה בָּרָה (instead of אַהֲבָתְךָ הַבָּרָה) is two syllables shorter and matches the tune's eight.

3:2 שָׂגַב מֵעַל הֶעָנָן — the Arabic فَاقَتْ سَمَتْ فَوْقَ الْغَمَام is 'surpassed, soared above the clouds'; שָׂגַב is the psalm's verb for being exalted (Ps 68:19, עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם), so the grace is high rather than merely large.

4:1–2 לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר כִּי תָּנוּחַ דַּעְתְּךָ — the Arabic مَا كَانَ إِمْكَانٌ بِأَنْ تَرْتَاحَ أَوْ تَهْدَأَ بَال is 'it was not possible that You should rest or be calm in mind'; the verbless אֶפְשָׁר is Mishnaic but the only word for 'possible', and it is kept because the line's subject is possibility, not permission.

6:3–4 הַשְׁלֵם … הַבְטָחַת בּוֹאֲךָ — the Arabic فَأَنْجِزَنَّ فِي الْمَسِيح وَعْدَ مَجِيئِهِ الْقَرِيب is 'fulfil in Christ the promise of His soon coming'; the Hebrew keeps 'in Christ' as the sphere of fulfilment, and the promise is phrased as 'Your coming', matching the print's shift from third to second person.
